mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 116i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 116i engine replacement typically costs £1,495-£2,600 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, depending on the engine code. With supply and fit, expect £2,300-£3,500 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 116i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 116i (N43 and N13 engines) include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 116i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2007-2015 BMW 1 Series 116i is typically valued at £2,000-£6,000. If your 116i is worth under £3,500, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £5,000+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 116i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 116i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 116i and 118i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 116i and 118i share engine families but with different power outputs. The 116i produces 109-136 hp depending on generation, while the 118i produces more power (up to 170 hp in later models). The 116i was positioned as the entry-level petrol model.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 116i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 116i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N43, N13 or B38 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 116i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 116i has been the entry-level petrol model across three generations of the 1 Series in the UK. Launched with the first-generation E87 in 2004, it has evolved from a naturally aspirated 1.6-litre four-cylinder to a turbocharged 1.6-litre, and finally to an efficient 1.5-litre three-cylinder. The 116i badge represents accessible BMW ownership without compromising the rear-wheel-drive dynamics the 1 Series is known for.

milestones.description: N45B16, 1.6L naturally aspirated I4, 115 hp, launched with the E87 five-door and E81 three-door 1 Series
N43B16, 1.6L naturally aspirated I4 with direct injection, 122 hp, introduced as part of the E87/E81 LCI update
N43B20, 2.0L naturally aspirated I4, 122 hp, replaces the 1.6L N43 in some markets
N13B16, 1.6L turbocharged I4, 136 hp, launched with the second-generation F20/F21 1 Series
B38B15, 1.5L turbocharged I3, 109 hp, introduced as part of the F20/F21 LCI update
F20/F21 generation ends; the 116i badge is discontinued in the UK

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 1 Series 116i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 116i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 116i has been powered by five different petrol engines across its production life, each with its own character and weaknesses. Early cars (2004-2007) use the N45B16 - a simple, reliable unit that can suffer from oil consumption. The N43 engines (2007-2012) introduced direct injection but brought timing chain guide fragility. The N13 turbo (2011-2015) offered more power but inherited timing chain problems. Later B38-powered cars (2015-2019) are the most reliable of the bunch. Replacement demand for the BMW 116i is driven primarily by N43 and N13 timing chain failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 116i N43 and N13 Engines Fail Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain guides on BMW's N43 and N13 petrol engines were made of plastic that becomes brittle with age and heat. The guides can break, allowing the chain to become slack. Because both engines are of interference type, a stretched or snapped timing chain can cause pistons to collide with valves - resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is already damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2015 BMW 1 Series 116i is currently valued at approximately £2,000-£6,000 depending on mileage, condition and generation. This places the 116i in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 116i is worth under £3,500 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage, later generation) worth £5,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic rattling noise from the timing chain on cold start in your N43 or N13-powered BMW 116i, act immediately. An £800-£1,300 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 116i for 2+ years, a reconditioned N43 or N13 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear - N45 and N43 Engines
problems.affectedModels: BMW 1 Series 116i (N45B16 / N43B16 / N43B20, high-mileage examples)
problems.rootCause: The N45 and N43 engines can suffer from worn valve stem seals, leading to excessive oil consumption. This is often accompanied by blue smoke on start-up and a gradual increase in oil usage between services.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals without removing cylinder head (specialist tooling)
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before other damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new seals, guides and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is severe and compression is low

problems.recommendation: Oil consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles or more warrants investigation. A specialist valve stem seal replacement using the "in-situ" method (without cylinder head removal) is often the most cost-effective solution for the BMW 1 Series 116i. If combined with timing chain wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components may offer better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 1 Series 116i engine prices

problems.h4: Coil Pack and Injector Failure - N43 Engine
problems.rootCause: The N43 engine's direct injection system is sensitive to carbon build-up and component wear. Coil packs and injectors can fail, causing misfires, rough running and reduced power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty coil packs and/or injectors
repairOptions.longevity: If misfire codes are present and engine runs rough

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If multiple components have failed and reliability is compromised

problems.recommendation: Coil pack and injector issues on the N43 are usually repairable without replacing the entire engine. A diagnostic scan will identify which cylinder is misfiring. Replace faulty components individually - this is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. However, if the timing chain is also showing signs of wear, consider the cumulative repair cost against a rebuilt engine.
